key_insight: Hydrogen multi-energy system operation is largely binary and driven by renewable surplus, with statistical and machine learning methods together revealing both linear and non-linear control signals.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports deployable dispatch controllers and operational threshold detection for H-MES, helping improve hydrogen production scheduling and revenue-oriented control.
method: Analyzed one year of high-resolution operational data from a hydrogen multi-energy system.
Used statistical tests, multiple regression, Random Forest, sequence modeling, and reinforcement learning.
Compared linear, rank-based, and temporal patterns to identify thresholds and forecasting signals.
evidence_signal: Solar irradiance explained 45.7% of rank-based variance in hydrogen production, while electrolyzer power was the strongest linear predictor and 24-hour autocorrelation was strong (r = 0.845).
watch_item: Results are data- and site-specific, so controller performance may vary when transferred to other H-MES configurations or operating regimes.
paper_title: A Statistical and Machine Learning Framework for Operational Threshold Detection and Deployable Dispatch Controller Development in Hydrogen Multi-Energy Systems
